semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1 and every real r with (n-1)/n <= r < 1, for every integer k with 1 <= k < n, the floor of k times r equals k minus 1; additionally, the floor of n times r equals n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with (n-1)/n <= r and r < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k and k < n
witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses; all quantities are asserted for given n and r and for every eligible k.

payload.statement_nl: Let n > 1 and let r be a real number with (n-1)/n <= r < 1. Then for every integer k with 1 <= k < n, floor(k*r) = k - 1, and also floor(n*r) = n - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be an integer and let r be a real number with (n - 1)/n <= r < 1.

First, let k be any integer with 1 <= k < n. From r < 1 we get kr < k. Also, since r >= (n - 1)/n, we have
kr >= k(n - 1)/n = k - k/n.
Because k < n and n > 0, we have k/n < 1, so k - k/n > k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 < kr < k.
Since k - 1 is an integer, this implies floor(kr) = k - 1.

Now take k = n. From r >= (n - 1)/n we get
nr >= n - 1,
and from r < 1 we get nr < n. Hence
n - 1 <= nr < n,
so floor(nr) = n - 1.

This proves that for every integer k with 1 <= k < n, floor(k r) = k - 1, and also floor(n r) = n - 1.
result_payload.proof_summary: Sandwich kr between k-1 and k for k<n, using (n-1)/n <= r < 1; then handle k=n similarly to obtain floor(nr)=n-1.
